subject.title: feat(session): add named new and close chat commands

question: Should OpenClaw expose `/close` and `/delete` as destructive session-management commands across chat channels, and if so should their user-facing contract distinguish archive from permanent incognito deletion?
rationale: The implementation adds a new cross-channel destructive command surface with different persistence outcomes by session type; code review can repair the mechanics, but maintainers must choose the durable user-facing contract.

options.title: Sponsor a precise close contract
options.body: Keep the commands, define truthful archive/delete wording and safeguards for every session type, then require the concrete lifecycle and proof fixes before merge.

options.title: Limit to existing UI actions
options.body: Do not add chat-side destructive commands; retain the established Control UI session-management surfaces instead.

options.title: Pause for a narrower proposal
options.body: Split naming from deletion and revisit chat closure with a dedicated UX and lifecycle design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a precise close contract
recommendation.body: Keep the commands, define truthful archive/delete wording and safeguards for every session type, then require the concrete lifecycle and proof fixes before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: BSG2000 has prior merged history in the adjacent chat session-command surface and is the clearest available routing candidate.
